jon: Heads-up — running long-context stress (seq_len ~32k) on H100 and seeing steady VRAM growth that never fully reclaims. Looks like KV cache paging churn + tiny evict waves. Repro below.
jon: repro:
```
./run_infer --model redwood-v1 --context 32000 --batch 4 --kernel-profile=on --kv-mode=paged
```
jon: snippet from logs: `kvcache: page_fault id=0x7f3 evict=1 idx=12345 reuse=0 iter=9876` repeated every ~200ms, and `pager: walk_ms=12 alloc_ms=0.8` spikes.
li: Hmm. Any correlation with kernel selection logs? which kernel was picked for attention (tiling vs streaming)?
jon: profiler shows we frequently switch between tiled_attn_small and stream_attn_large mid-run when token distribution shifts — kernel-selector log toggles around the same time as spike in page faults.
mira: That smells like we end up allocating different tiling layouts and fragmenting the page table mapping. If the kernel switches, the KV layout/stride changes and may cause holes that prevent reuse.
sam: I ran a quick compare on MI250X with same workload — fewer page_faults but higher fragmentation count in telemetry (frag_runs:+12%). So arch differences matter. H100 shows more evict churn, MI250X shows long-lived tiny holes.
dana: Could batching heuristics be worsening it? if batch token mix oscillates, selector flips kernels and we lose contiguous KV extents.
li: Can you paste the kernel-selector trace (timestamps) and kvcache metrics aligned? even 10 lines would help.
jon: Pasted minimal alignment:
```
5478901234 kernel=tiling_small
5478901236 kvcache: page_fault idx=12345
5478901240 kernel=stream_large
5478901242 kvcache: page_fault idx=12347
5478901246 kvcache: evict idx=12345
```
jon: Note how page_faults coincide with kernel flips.
mira: Quick hypothesis: selector toggles kernel which changes per-token KV stride -> allocator splits extent -> eviction heuristics use LRU that forgets about small reuse windows -> thrash.
sam: Repro plan: force kernel=tiling_small for full run and compare evict/sec and peak_vram. If peak significantly lower then kernel selection is culprit.
dana: Also try increasing `kvcache.prefetch_window` and raising `max_batch_tokens` to reduce flip frequency.
li: If this is true, possible fixes: 1) make kernel selection stable for a given context length/sequence distribution, 2) align allocator to canonical KV stride to avoid splitting, or 3) make eviction coalesce nearby extents when stride toggles.
jon: I ran forced-kernel run: peak_vram -8% and evicts/sec -60%. So forcing stability helps.
infra-bot: perf-job triggered: `kvcache/kernel-stability/5478901234` — running forced-kernel vs auto for H100 and MI250X. Job link: https://ci.internal/perf/5478901234
dana: Nice. Let's triage options: short-term -> pin kernel for long-context mode; mid-term -> allocator coalescing + selector hysteresis; long-term -> telemetry regression to detect flip->evict correlation and auto-hold kernel for N tokens.
mira: I'll draft a minimal allocator patch that prefers contiguous extents for small-stride variants. Will open PR and attach microbench.
jon: Thanks — I'll attach the failed trace and raw profiler to the perf job. For now marking as p0 for runtime perf.
